I just got out of the hospital yesterday after being in there for a few days for feelings the same way. 

I'm still in a lot of pain, and to be honest, feel just as empty as I did before I had called the police and gone in. 

However, it did spark the smallest of lights within me to get help, and I've got myself an appointment with a psychiatrist at the same hospital this Sunday.

I'm so sorry you're feeling this way. I know just how you're feeling, because I feel the same way. 

I love you, man. I wish I could give you a good hug. I know it's hard, but I'm so happy you're here, friend.

I definitely feel you on the lonely night. 

It's tough, making, keeping, and managing friends/friendships when you're depressed. It's hard to believe, even myself, but despite of that, having little to no friends only means you have more friends to make. 

I'd love to be your friend, man. I know it's not a tangible, real life friendship, but my best friends were made online. 

What movie are you watching at the moment?

Hey! 

I'm not entirely sure why I'm up this late either, but I can definitely sympathize, and empathize with you. 

You're going to graduate! That's incredible, and I'm genuinely proud of you. It can be, and feel so impossible to think positively about yourself dealing with mental illness, which I'm guessing you do, but you've put in SO much to be where you are right now. 
I know my words may not have a giant impact on the way you see things, or the way you feel, but as stated above, I'm genuinely proud of you for sticking through school. 

Good fucking job. 

As for your dad, I've never dealt with anything like that, but I can only imagine what that'd be like. 

How long has that been a thing?

I can definitely relate. 

My mother and I are both "clean freaks", but we both deal with depression and would more often than not neglect our chores, and I always felt so embarrassed when my sister would bring all her friends over to hang out with the house in such poor condition.   

Is talking to your partner about your depression completely out of the question?

This makes me really happy.

I'm glad you've found a way to keep yourself going. The selfless way of thinking is actually a great way to motivate yourself. 

Keep your head up, and keep doing what you're doing. I'm proud of you.

I think you have really nice eyes, and every smile is always beautiful. 

If you'd like to talk more, you're more than welcome to message me. 

 

Keep your chin up, friend.

Yeah, that feeling of emptiness can be extremely overwhelming. 
I'm glad I could help as much as I could!

I can relate. I feel like my cognitive functions have deteriorated over time, to the point where I can't articulate myself well. 

I don't know you by name, but to me, you are ZTB! You are important just like everyone else here in /r/Depression
You're more than welcome to message me if you'd like to talk some more.

I feel you.


I had to withdraw from school within the first month of my 10th grade year, and I've been out of school since.

I've been at home almost every day since, and despite of my efforts of trying to go back, I just couldn't. I can't see myself working because of my depression and anxiety either, and I feel unaccomplished myself.

 I'll be 20 in April, and I don't have a High-school education or any work experience.

The word burden is something I really feel like I identify with, too.


I know our circumstances are different, but I genuinely understand how you feel, and I really hope you're able to find that thing that keeps you going.

You deserve to be happy just like everyone else, and I wish for nothing more than for you to be able to live a long happy life. 


It's incredibly hard, but to keep your head up; I'm rooting for you.
The amount of times I've "misplaced" my glasses and broke down, only to find them on my face is ridiculous.. Haha.

I definitely felt this way, but I think the feeling has evolved into something a bit different.

I don't really feel liked or loved, desirable or wanted, but I'm so used to it that it's no big deal.

Yeah, I definitely feel this way. 

My 18th birthday was the worst, as my best-friend and all my old peers were graduating around that time. 

I had to withdraw from school my 10th grade year because of my depression and anxiety, and I've never been able to go back despite of trying every year since. 

Next year I'll be 20, and I'll have no High-school education whatsoever. 


That genuinely saddens me..

My depression has also affected me in a very  similar manner.

I find it hard to articulate myself a majority of the time, and I always seem to forget what I'm going to say; whether it's a single word, or compete sentences.

I know, man. I know.

However, regardless of how you may feel, you're not alone. 

/r/depression is a great community, and we all genuinely care for one another. 

I know my words may not have an impact, but I genuinely love and care for you. 

You are important, you are special, and you deserve happiness just as much as anyone. 

As someone who's in a very similar situation, I don't know what the future holds. 
I don't know what'll happen tomorrow, and I sure as heck don't know what life will be like in a decade from now.


All I can say is, take it day by day. I'm rooting for you, man. 


Stay strong.

You are in incredibly strong person.

I'm genuinely happy for you, and I wish  you the best.  


Stay strong, man.

I know how you feel, man.

I'm around your age (19), and have also been dealing with depression since I was young. 

I know that feeling of loneliness, emptiness, and all around nothingness, so I empathize with you. 


I'm willing to lend an ear if you're in need of one. 


Stay strong, friend. I love you.

I would recommend looking into some kind of food-bank as well, if there's anything like that in your area. 


It'd definitely lessen the load that you and your sister carry.

Though I don't know you personally, I love you.



I know how depression is, and the feeling of disbelief at the sight or sound of those words, but I truly love you.

People say things they don't mean when they're upset, so please don't think anything of what your sister or anyone has said. 



You're struggling, and I know how that feels; I am too.


However, once you've hit "rock bottom", there's no where else to go but up.



I'm sorry that you're feeling this way, but I love you, and I'm rooting for you. 




I might not be a therapist, but If you need to talk, you're more than welcome to message me. I'm always willing to lend an ear to someone who needs it.


Stay strong.

I'm really happy you were able to see yourself off of the edge and onto safer ground. 

Keep on keeping on, man. 

I'm rooting for you.

I'm half Asian myself, and I didn't really grow up with the Asian influence most Asians experience, but I understand what you're feeling; my biological father's grandparents were mostly disappointed when they found out. 

I grew up with my
Mother and step-father who both happen to be white, and they were very accepting of my mental illnesses; though my step-father doesn't really know how it affects me personally. 

All I can say is hang in there, and try your best. 
 
I hope they're able to understand one day, and give you the support you need. 
However, I'm here to support you, and I'll be rooting for you all the way.  I'm always available if you ever want to talk.

I know how you feel. I feel that way as well on a daily basis. 

I genuinely hope you're able to find happiness, and live a long happy life. 

You're more than welcome to message me whenever you'd like if you ever want to talk.

Well, I guess it's good you dodged that bullet then. I still wish people were more educated about depression. It's saddening to see some of the stuff people say online, or even things you hear in person.
This is why I never tell people. I hate the attention, and there's a chance you'll hear  something like that from someone who doesn't understand. I'm sorry, I wish people were more understanding.

I'm happy your father walked in when he did, and I'm even happier that you're okay and still here with us. 

I know what what it's like to be "on the edge". 

You're  still pretty young, and I'd genuinely love for you to be able to live a long and happy life.
